name: MonarchButtonStyle
title: SplitButton
wrapsNative: Menu(content:label:primaryAction:) with .buttonStyle(.monarch(_:size:)); or an HStack of a Button and an icon-only Menu, both with .buttonStyle(.monarch(_:))
summary: A main action joined to a menu of alternatives, such as Save with Save as draft and Save and close: the standard Menu with a primary action and the Monarch button style.
whenToUse: When one action is the usual choice and a few related alternatives are needed now and then.
whenNotToUse: When no action is the default, use a menu button (Menu without primaryAction). When the alternatives are as common as the main action, show them as separate buttons.
api: Menu(content: () -> Content, label: () -> Label, primaryAction: () -> Void)
func buttonStyle(_ style: MonarchButtonStyle) -> some View  // .monarch(_ variant: MonarchButtonVariant = .secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, fullWidth: Bool = false)

options.name: variant
options.description: On .buttonStyle(.monarch(_:size:fullWidth:)): primary, secondary, ghost or danger. Use ghost for an icon-only trigger.

options.name: size
options.description: sm, md or lg. The touch target is at least 44 points at every size.

options.name: fullWidth
options.description: Whether the trigger fills the available width.

states.name: idle
states.description: One Monarch button. A tap runs the main action; a long press opens the alternatives.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The pressed colour of the variant.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(true) disables the main action and the menu together. In the joined recipe, disable the arrow alone to keep the main action available.

appearance: The colours of the chosen Monarch button variant. The joined recipe draws two buttons of the same variant two points apart; the menu is the system's, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web SplitButton draws the main button and a separate arrow button with its own Tab stop and the name "More options for <label>". iOS's own idiom is Menu with primaryAction: one button, a tap for the main action and a long press for the alternatives, as in Mail and Safari. Because the long press is not visible, the second recipe joins a main button to a visible arrow Menu when the alternatives must be found by everyone. The web menuDisabled maps to disabling the arrow in that recipe. Android ships a MonarchSplitButton type.
accessibility: With primaryAction, VoiceOver activates the main action with a double tap and offers the menu in the actions rotor (system behaviour).
In the joined recipe the arrow is a separate element named "More options for <title>" by accessibilityLabel, and the pair is a container named after the main action.
Each button keeps a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: A long press on a disabled Menu does nothing.
The long-press menu is not discoverable by sight; use the joined recipe when that matters.
On macOS (host builds only) Menu with primaryAction draws a split pull-down; iOS is the supported platform.
How VoiceOver announces the long-press menu was not checked on a device.
